summary: Multicast VPN routes in BGP carry addresses from both the customer's and the provider's address spaces, which are independent and may use different IP versions. This RFC specifies how the address family of provider infrastructure addresses is encoded so IPv4 and IPv6 can be handled correctly.

eli5.summary: Customer and provider each have their own address books, which can use old or new style addresses. This makes sure the message says clearly which kind of address it is using.

questions: ipv4 and ipv6 in multicast vpn
how are ipv6 addresses carried in mvpn bgp routes
subtitle: Provider router addresses in multicast VPN BGP routes are told apart as IPv4 or IPv6 by their length, not by the route's address family field.

tldr.problem: Multicast VPN routes in BGP carry customer addresses and provider router addresses, and the two can use different IP versions. The route's address family field only describes the customer side.
tldr.mechanism: Whenever a provider edge router address appears in an MCAST-VPN route, its IP version is read from its length: 4 octets means IPv4 and 16 octets means IPv6. The RFC also sets how IPv6 addresses go in the VRF Route Import extended community and how PMSI Tunnel attributes relate to the next hop.
tldr.outcome: Implementations can interoperate when an IPv4 provider network serves IPv6 customers, or the other way round. The RFC updates RFC 6514.

facts.label: IANA code point
facts.value: 0x000b (VRF Route Import, IPv6 Address Specific Extended Community)

today: RFC 6515 is a Proposed Standard published in February 2012. It updates RFC 6514, and no later RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Two Address Spaces, One Route
sections.content:
Service providers offer Multicast VPN (MVPN) service using BGP routes of a new type, carried with the MCAST-VPN NLRI. The NLRI travels inside the MP_REACH_NLRI and MP_UNREACH_NLRI attributes, and the SAFI field marks it as MCAST-VPN.

For these routes the AFI field has two values. AFI 1 means the customer multicast addresses are IPv4, and AFI 2 means they are IPv6. But some routes also hold addresses of Provider Edge (PE) routers, which live in the provider's own address space. An IPv4 provider network can serve IPv6 customers and an IPv6 provider network can serve IPv4 customers, so the PE address family MUST NOT be inferred from the AFI field.
sections.eli5: The customer's address book and the provider's address book are separate, and they can be different styles. So the label on the customer's book cannot tell you the style of the provider's book.

sections.title: Length Decides the Address Family
sections.content:
The rule of this RFC is that whenever a PE address occurs in an MCAST-VPN route, in the NLRI or in an attribute, its family is set by its length: 4 octets for IPv4 and 16 octets for IPv6. If a provider with an IPv4 core serves IPv6 customers, the PE addresses are 4-octet IPv4 addresses even though the AFI of those routes is 2.

Earlier specifications (RFC 4659 and RFC 4798) took a different approach and required IPv4 PE addresses to be written as IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses in routes with IPv6 customer addresses. This RFC does not do that. It follows the approach of RFC 4684 and RFC 5549 instead.
sections.eli5: You count the digits in the address. A short one is the old style and a long one is the new style, no matter what the customer's label says.

sections.title: Where PE Addresses Appear
sections.content:
The RFC lists four places where a PE address occurs and how to work out its length in each.

  • The Network Address of Next Hop field in MP_REACH_NLRI. It has a length field in front of it, so a length of 4 means IPv4 and 16 means IPv6.
  • The Intra-AS I-PMSI A-D route. After the 1-octet route type, the 1-octet NLRI length and an 8-octet Route Distinguisher comes the Originating Router's IP Address. Its length follows from the NLRI length, which is 12 for IPv4 or 24 for IPv6.
  • The S-PMSI A-D route, where the address length is computed from the NLRI length and the lengths of the variable-length multicast source and group fields.
  • The Leaf A-D route, where it is computed from the NLRI length and the route key length.

In every case, if the length is neither 4 nor 16, the MP_REACH_NLRI attribute MUST be treated as incorrect and handled as RFC 4760 specifies.
sections.eli5: In each kind of message there is a way to measure how long the provider address is. If it is not one of the two allowed lengths, the whole message is thrown out as broken.

sections.title: The VRF Route Import Extended Community
sections.content:
The VRF Route Import Extended Community is attached to unicast VPN-IPv4 or VPN-IPv6 routes. As defined in RFC 6514 it is an IPv4 Address Specific Extended Community, so it can only carry an IPv4 address.

To carry an IPv6 address, an IPv6 Address Specific Extended Community (RFC 5701) of type VRF Route Import must be used. This holds whether the attribute is attached to a VPN-IPv4 or a VPN-IPv6 route.
sections.eli5: The old envelope only fits a short address. For a long address you need a bigger envelope, and this RFC says to use it.

sections.title: PMSI Tunnel Attributes
sections.content:
A PMSI Tunnel Attribute in an I-PMSI A-D route names the tunnel that a PE or ASBR uses by default for the multicast traffic of one customer MVPN. Two rules govern its meaning.

First, the AFI of the MP_REACH_NLRI says which traffic the tunnel carries: AFI 1 for IPv4 MVPN traffic and AFI 2 for IPv6. To assign both to an I-PMSI tunnel, two I-PMSI A-D routes MUST be used, one with AFI 1 and one with AFI 2. They can carry the same PMSI Tunnel attribute value if the same tunnel is used for both.

Second, the next hop sets the tunnel address family. If the next hop is an IPv4 address, any IP addresses in the Tunnel Identifier field MUST be IPv4. If it is IPv6, they MUST be IPv6. A mismatch makes the attribute a malformed PMSI Tunnel Attribute, as RFC 6514 specifies.
sections.eli5: The customer label says what kind of traffic rides the tunnel. The provider address style has to match the tunnel's own addresses, or the message is rejected.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content:
IANA assigned the code point 0x000b for VRF Route Import in the IPv6 Address Specific Extended Community registry, in the transitive communities part of the namespace. The references are this document and RFC 6514.

The security section says the document raises no security considerations beyond those of RFC 6514.
sections.eli5: A new number was reserved in a public list so everyone uses the same code for the bigger envelope. Nothing new is risky here.
